overview: Frontend Engineers specialize in creating intuitive, responsive user interfaces and client-side web applications using modern web standards and frameworks.
learning_roadmap: Master HTML5 semantic layout, modern CSS flexbox/grid, and responsive mobile-first design.
Deep dive into vanilla JavaScript (closures, asynchronous async/await, DOM manipulation, ES modules).
Learn TypeScript fundamentals for scalable enterprise application codebases.
Specialize in React 18, hook lifecycles (useState, useEffect, useMemo), state managers, and component architecture.
Understand build tooling (Vite, Webpack), package management (npm), and CI/CD basics.
interview_topics: Virtual DOM vs Real DOM and React reconciliation mechanism.
State management trade-offs (Context API vs Redux Toolkit vs Zustand).
CSS specificity, box model, and CSS-in-JS vs utility-first Tailwind CSS.
Performance optimization: Code splitting, lazy loading, image optimization, memoization.
Web accessibility (a11y) standards and semantic HTML.
diu_campus_advice: Join DIU Computer & Programming Club (CPC), build portfolio projects hosted on Vercel/GitHub Pages, and participate in campus hackathons.

overview: Backend Engineers architect reliable server-side systems, design relational and NoSQL databases, construct secure REST/GraphQL APIs, and manage business logic.
learning_roadmap: Master a primary backend language such as Python (FastAPI/Django) or JavaScript/TypeScript (Node.js/Express).
Deeply study relational database design, normalization, ACID properties, indexing, and query optimization.
Implement secure authentication patterns (OAuth2, JWT, Bcrypt password hashing, RBAC).
Containerize microservices using Docker and write multi-container Docker Compose definitions.
Learn asynchronous programming, background tasks (Celery, RQ), and caching strategies with Redis.
interview_topics: Database indexing: B-trees, hash indexes, composite keys, and EXPLAIN query analysis.
RESTful API design principles and HTTP status code semantics.
Concurrency, async I/O event loops, and thread pools.
Session management vs stateless JWT bearer authentication.
System design basics: Load balancers, caching layers, database replication, and rate limiting.
diu_campus_advice: Focus heavily on DIU's Database Management Systems (DBMS) and Object Oriented Programming (OOP) courses. Build robust CRUD APIs with automated tests.

overview: Full-Stack Engineers bridge the client and server sides, delivering complete end-to-end web products from database schemas up to responsive user interfaces.
learning_roadmap: Build strong foundations in both frontend web components and backend RESTful architectures.
Implement unified full-stack projects combining React with FastAPI or Node.js.
Learn deployment workflows, environment variable configurations, and automated testing.
Develop deep appreciation for UX/UI usability combined with backend throughput and latency.
interview_topics: Full request-response cycle from browser DNS lookup to server database execution.
CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) mechanisms and preflight OPTIONS requests.
API contracts and data validation between frontend forms and backend models.
Monolith vs microservices trade-offs and full-stack deployment architectures.
diu_campus_advice: Your DIU Capstone Project is your primary portfolio showcase for local tech recruiters at Brain Station 23, BJIT, and Enosis.

overview: UI/UX Designers conduct user research, create wireframes and high-fidelity prototypes, and construct coherent design systems that make software delightful and accessible.
learning_roadmap: Master Figma tools: Auto-layout, components, variants, variables, and interactive prototyping.
Study human-computer interaction (HCI) fundamentals and Nielsen Norman usability heuristics.
Conduct user interviews, persona mapping, and empathy-driven user journey mapping.
Collaborate with engineering teams by understanding technical layout constraints and design handoffs.
interview_topics: Walkthrough of a case study showcasing discovery, user research, wireframing, and final outcome.
Design systems governance, tokenization, and developer handoff best practices.
Accessibility guidelines (WCAG 2.1 AA contrast ratios, screen reader compatibility).
Handling constructive feedback and user testing anomalies.
diu_campus_advice: Participate in UI/UX design competitions organized by the DIU Multimedia & Creative Technology (MCT) and CSE clubs.
